Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week. We have a fairly strict regulatory constraint for our upcoming telehealth pilot: all inference must execute and remain resident in EU (prefer eu-west-1), and we cannot allow automatic fallback to any model variant or to other regions.

Specifically:
- We need a binding that pins requests to a single model variant (sha/identifier will be provided) and prevents Redwood from routing to other variants without written approval.
- No automatic cross-region fallback under any capacity conditions (even transient outages). If the model is unavailable, requests should fail rather than route elsewhere.
- Data residency: logs, KV cache, and any short-term caches must remain in EU-controlled storage, with keys managed under our KMS.

Attached is our compliance sheet with the required contractual language and an architecture sketch (healthgrid_compliance_requirements.xlsx). Procurement is copied. Can you confirm whether this is feasible on Redwood Hosted, or do we need Dedicated or Private? Also share rough timelines and any additional evidence (SOC2, data flow diagrams).

Tina

Thanks Sean. Quick operational notes from CS side:
- For pilots with regulatory constraints we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private because Hosted has routing automation that can be hard to fully disable today.
- If HealthGrid insists on Hosted, we need a documented, tested runbook and SLA carveouts that define expected behavior during capacity issues (fail-closed behavior, incident comms, and a compensation model).
- KMS: we can integrate their customer-managed keys for data-at-rest in Dedicated and Private; Hosted support for CMK is limited to specific enterprise tiers.
- KV cache residency: we must ensure that ephemeral caches and any prefix caching are pinned to EU-only hosts; that’s currently configurable but would require an audit and a validation plan.

Two clarifying questions for Tina:
1) When you say "no fallback," do you mean (A) we may never route to an alternate model variant in any scenario, or (B) we can have a human-approved emergency fallback process with 24-hour notice?
2) Is eu-west-1 a hard requirement, or is any EU region acceptable as long as it remains within EU jurisdiction?

Operationally, options:
A) Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 with pinned model variant and strict routing policy enforced by Ops (recommended short-term).
B) Private deployment (highest assurance) — longer lead time and different commercial model.

Irene / Product: can you summarize what is feasible immediately vs needs engineering changes (and approximate ETA)?

—Priya
Senior Customer Success Manager

Subject: Re: EU-only inference + strict no-fallback / model binding

Short answer: technically feasible with caveats.

Feasibility summary:
- Region lock: yes. We can enforce route policies that bind traffic to a region (eu-west-1) at the edge/router layer.
- Model binding: yes. We can pin a customer to a model artifact (immutable variant id) and prevent automatic variant selection.
- No-fallback enforcement: we can set a strict policy that fails requests when the pinned variant is not available instead of falling back. That behavior exists in our runtime as a policy flag, but it is not currently exposed to Hosted customers as a self-serve toggle.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Availability: fail-closed means the customer sees errors when we run out of capacity or a host/zone outage occurs. This increases outage exposure compared to our typical multi-region/fallback architecture.
- Operational burden: we need a dedicated capacity reservation and an on-call mitigation plan (auto-alerts, capacity warmers).
- Cost: dedicated capacity + reserved nodes will raise unit costs (rough estimate +20-35% per token depending on model size).

Mitigations / recommended path:
1) Short-term (immediate): Stand up a small Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 with an enforced routing policy (Ops + Infra). Use pinned variant and set runtime policy to fail-closed. Provide HealthGrid with a validation runbook and a time-window SLA for incidents (e.g., 4 hr incident response for pilot). This can be done within ~2 weeks with Ops prioritization.
2) Mid-term (6–8 weeks): Expose a Hosted enterprise toggle for "strict no-fallback" and region binding with audit logs and KMS support. This requires product & infra work (INF-9223).
3) Long-term: Private deployment option for regulated customers with full CMK + air-gap support.

Suggested contract clause language for procurement: "Redwood will not route inference requests for HealthGrid outside the European Union or to alternate model variants without prior written authorization from HealthGrid. In the event of a capacity or infrastructure outage that prevents processing in the designated region and pinned model variant, Redwood will (a) promptly notify HealthGrid per the incident communication plan; and (b) offer remediation options including priority capacity or paid failover only with explicit HealthGrid approval."

Next steps:
- Ops: create a Dedicated pool proposal (size: small pilot, 2–4 reserved workers) and cost estimate.
- Legal/Revenue: review suggested clause. Marissa, can you start redlines?
- CS: prepare validation script/checklist and scheduled test window with HealthGrid. Priya, can you own that?

Irene: I'll link INF-9223 for tracking.

Karthik Iyer
Group PM, Inference & Runtime
